en: Are you sure you were even wearing it? Maybe you never even put it on that day.
If I hadn't, it'd be in my closet, but it ain't there.
Oh, right. Maybe you really did take it off and leave it somewhere then.
This really sucks. I'm never gonna have too much to drink again!
Anyone ever tell ya you've got a nice voice, Akiyama-san?
Sometimes. Though honestly I'm not too sure of that myself.
When I hear my own voice in a recording, I just think about how weird it sounds.
I hear that! I remember bein' real upset when I first heard my own voice.
No, not really. I guess you'd be the first.
Really? But ya've got a great voice! Lately, I make a point to pay attention to a man's voice, and yers has a nice ring to it, Akiyama-san!
Well, I'm happy to hear it.
I wanna be a newscaster, y'know.
A newscaster? Wow, you've chosen a pretty tough career path.
I'm goin' to school and takin' lessons, but my accent's givin' me a lotta trouble.
What's wrong with an accent? Other regional dialects can be problematic, but most people can handle Kansai-ben.
No way! There ain't no newscasters who read broadcast news in a regional dialect!
Not even comedians on variety programs use their dialect when hostin' their shows.
Now that you mention it, I guess nationally broadcasted shows don't do dialects, do they?
It's not that ya can't use it, but why use words that are difficult to understand? If ya know standard Japanese, might as well use it.
I gotcha.
You're overthinking things. Your success as a newscaster doesn't hinge only on that. Why don't you work on improving your other skills first?
Huh? But what if I don't wind up bein' able to fix my accent in the long run?
Maybe you should try to immerse yourself in the Tokyo accent, so you get more used to it.
I guess so. But when I'm here at work, I keep hearin' Kansai-ben all the time, whether I wanna or not. So I'm not sure how I'm gonna do that.
I could teach you. I have a good ear for that sort of thing, so if you get the accent wrong I'll point it out for you.
Ya mean it? That'd be tops if you could do it! Much obliged to ya, Akiyama-san!
Yeah, well, in your case, maybe your accent isn't the primary thing to worry about...
That's an excuse. If this job is an issue, you should quit and work somewhere else. If you want to make your dreams come true, give it your all.
Hey! I get what you're sayin' but it ain't exactly that simple! I don't like ya suggestin' that I ain't prepared to give my all, either!
I figured you'd say that. It's a tricky thing, making your dreams come true.
What about TV stations in Kansai? I'm sure there must be plenty of big networks here in Osaka where having an accent wouldn't be an issue.
Yeah, but I wanna work for a national network.
So you want to get a broadcasting job in Tokyo?
Yeah, that's why I wanna fix my accent.
I see. But from what I've heard from you, you're not trying to hide the accent much. Your Kansai-ben is pretty thick.
You have to make a point to use the standard Japanese accent daily.
Yer right.
If I'm reading text it's fine, but I talk faster than I think, so most o' the time it's Kansai-ben that winds up comin' outta my mouth.
You're at least aware of the issue. Now you need to work on it. You need to try to think with a standard dialect while you're speaking.
Okay! I'm gonna do my best!
It's going to be a long road ahead of you.
Why's a national network better?
Because that's where I'll get better exposure. Ya can't compare the fame of a national show to somethin' local to Osaka.
True enough. Still, you need to be pretty ruthless to make it in the world of television.
I hear ya there. I'm gonna be a household name, no matter what!
Well, you certainly don't lack tenacity.
Whoa, hey. A newscaster isn't the same thing as an entertainer. What's the point of standing out when your job is to report the news?
Well yeah, but lately female newscasters are like idols, y'know? Some of 'em have even released photo books!
I suppose that's true. Maybe that's something the broadcast industry is looking for now.
Okay. I'll try not to butt in where my opinion isn't warranted.
You look sleepy. Were you up all last night?
Oh, sorry 'bout that. I wasn't up all night, but I didn't sleep all that much.
I was gonna kill time at a manga café while I waited for the mornin' train, but I fell asleep and had to go right to class and then here to work.
You're pushing yourself hard. You need to rest or you'll wreck your health.
Well, I can't take time off from work or I'll get hit with a penalty. But that's typical for a hostess. The girls will laugh at me if I whine 'bout it.
I want to commend that gung-ho attitude, but not being able to vent is a big warning sign. You shouldn't push yourself too hard.
Stop whining. You at least got a nap in, right? Newscasters wake up early and work late for broadcasts, so lack of sleep is part of the job.
I hear ya! I'm probably just sleepy 'cause I'm low on energy. I'll try to kick it up!
Well, don't overexert yourself.
I know why you're working so hard at school, but why are you pushing your hostess work so hard, too? Are you that strapped for cash?
Yeah. Ya can never have too much money when you're aimin' to be a newscaster.
I gotta pay for newscaster school tuition, and I gotta buy all my own clothes and makeup, too. Looks are important for ladies in broadcastin'.
Very true. I guess female newscasters can't live the life of a poor, starving student.
Yeah! And since I don't have a target amount I'm savin' up for, I can't just work a quick stint and quit.
Do you want to quit?
Well, yeah. Once I finally make it big as a reporter, the tabloids'll print stories about how I used to work as a hostess.
In that case, why are you working as a hostess? There's nothing good about it.
'Cause I need the money! Most folks who hafta take classes to get into their line a' work take on night jobs of some sort to get the cash.
Quite true. It's kind of ironic.
You don't need to quit. There's nothing bad about having money, and you're better off making money while you can.
Yeah. If I get hired by a company in Tokyo, my commute is gonna cost me an arm and a leg, so I gotta save up even more.
Right! I gotta hit the pavement a little harder! This money's gonna take me places!
You're definitely not lacking in enthusiasm.
Why don't you set a goal? That way, you can switch to a work shift that isn't so hard.
Hmm. I dunno about that. If I set my goal to make half a million yen a month, I'd wind up workin' every day anyway.
Okay, I understand that, but wouldn't it be good to have at least some kind of end-game in mind?
For me, that might wind up makin' me lazy. It's better for me to work as much as possible every day.
I see. In that case, just try not to push yourself so hard that you ruin your health.
Money isn't everything. If your goal is to become a newscaster, you should focus more on doing what it takes to make that a reality.
Huh? I'm not sure I get what you're sayin'. Are ya tellin' me to quit my hostess job?
Yes. I get that you need the money, but if the hostess lifestyle wears you down, all your effort will be for naught.
Although it doesn't pay as much, why don't you try part-time work that's a bit related to being a newscaster... like working in a call center?
Hey, mind yer own business! I'm already studyin' hard enough to be a newscaster. I don't need my side job to overlap with that.
I'm tired enough as it is, so don't go sayin' stuff that's gonna make me even crankier!
I can see I've crossed a line here. I'm sorry.
No. Quite the opposite.
The opposite? How do ya mean?
Working as a hostess isn't just letting you save money. You're also in a position to pick up some skills you'll need to be a newscaster.
You know how to make a good first impression, how to carry yourself, and have good fashion sense. Those are all relevant to being a newscaster.
Oh yeah! They're super related!
See? Don't think of tending to your customers as simply a money-making opportunity. Think of it as a way to get valuable life experience.
That's a real good point ya got there, Akiyama-san! I'll try to keep that in mind!
What's the matter? Sleepy again?
Nah, it's just school stuff. My teacher got all super-critical on me.
Cheer up. It's not like you to be this down.
Bein' like me is what's makin' me so upset.
...What do you mean?
No matter how hard I try, I can't fix my accent. At this rate. I'm never gonna be able to become a newscaster in Tokyo.
Maybe not. Overcoming one's accent is something anyone from the countryside needs to do to be a newscaster. It's not a simple thing to get past.
But I'm the only one who's havin' issues. Other people can do it just fine, so why can't I?
Nuh-uh. You just need to practice harder.
Wow, what's wrong with you? Nuh-uh? Seriously?
Akiyama-san, ya sound like a girl.
...So, we were talking about your accent, yes?
Let me hear you. I'll be able to point out anything I hear that sounds off.
What!? Ya can't put me on the spot like that. There ain't no way I can just up and do it.
I promise to be honest. You came to me looking for help with this, right?
Okay. Thanks, Akiyama-san. All right, listen up.
I'm kidding. Still, it's definitely a critical problem if you're going to school and can't change your accent.
Maybe you need to get used to hearing the Tokyo accent more often.
I watch the news all the time.
But the stuff they say on the news is different from what folks talk 'bout normally, so I don't have much opportunity to use what I learned.
I suppose so. Even if you can read a script fine, that won't fix your normal way of speaking.
Don't ya think I know that!? I need you to think of what I can do to fix it!
Huh? You need me to think of a way?
You speak with a good Tokyo accent, Akiyama-san. Don't ya know any methods?
Force yourself to use it. It's just like learning a language like English or Chinese. You learn by speaking it. Come on, give it a shot.
Seriously? Okay. Ya promise you're gonna listen carefully?
Try watching other shows. Shows that feature more colloquial conversations.
Like what sort? Soap operas?
Soap operas are dialogue-heavy, but scripted. And that doesn't really represent the way people actually talk.
Maybe watch a Japanese class? The kind that they air on the education channels.
Huh? But aren't those meant for foreigners?
Maybe it'd help to get back to basics.
Hmm. That might actually work. I'll hafta give it a shot.
Last night, a man from Tokyo was arrested at a club in Sotenbori, Osaka for attemptin' to forcibly kiss a female employee while drunk.
In response to the police investigation, the suspect claims to have no memory of the incident due to intoxication and refutes all charges.
How was that?
That was perfect.
Liar! There was definitely an accent there! If ya ain't honest with me, I'll never get better! Don't try to spare my feelin's, okay?
Sorry. That wasn't my intention. Maybe I've got a bit of an accent myself?
There was a hint of an accent. Someone from Tokyo would hear it right away.
I figured as much.
But just a hint. I'm sure with a little more effort, you'll be able to speak just fine.
Ya mean it? That's super! Thanks for helpin' me out with this, Akiyama-san.
I'm happy to help where I can.
Are you talking about me?
Never ya mind that! Answer the question!
You said ya were gonna really be listenin'...
So I've got my first corporate hirin' test comin' up.
Wow, there are companies already starting up employment exams? Those keep getting earlier.
This first one ain't for a place out in Tokyo, though. It's for a station here in Osaka.
So this is kind of a backup for you? I guess it'll be good for helping you get used to the interview process.
If only it were that easy...
I'm still no good with my Tokyo accent. So I can't fail this one since I might have a better chance of gettin' a job here in Osaka.
That's important. You have to approach this like it's the real deal.
I have a feelin' I'm gonna slip up durin' the test. I wish I'd applied to other companies before this one, too.
Stay calm. If you go into it with the attitude that it's okay if you fail, you won't be as nervous. And you'll be able to show your true potential.
